subject: Dedicated capacity: burst escrow & autoscale policy for Peregrine Robotics
messages:

Subject: Sizing for Dedicated pool + short bursts

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. As we start mapping production traffic, a couple of asks from our infra and procurement teams: we need a recommended dedicated-capacity sizing for our initial rollout (global fleet control, ~300k inference calls/day; median prompt length ~120 tokens, peak hourly spike ~8x), and a clear policy for short-duration bursts (10-30 minutes) without immediate overprovisioning.

Can you share a model for headroom and an example of how Redwood would handle a rapid spike (eviction, preemption, and billing)? Also, procurement will want an appendix describing credits/escrow for bursts.

If helpful, I can share our weekly traffic CSV.

— Amy
Infra Lead, Peregrine Robotics

Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated pool + short bursts

Amy — thanks, this is helpful. I pulled together an initial sizing and an ops pattern that balances cost predictability with burst flexibility. High level:

- Baseline reserved slab: 12 GPUs (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) sized for steady-state 1.5x median load.
- Shoulder buffer: 3 GPUs provisioned as hot-standby (fast prewarm).
- Ephemeral burst pool: access to up to +24 GPUs on burst (subject to regional availability). Bursts are time-limited and gated by burst credits.
- Autoscale policy: 2-tier scaling — fast lane (0–60s scaling for latency-sensitive routes using prewarmed shoulder) and slow lane (3–8 min for bulk/throughput routes).

I attached a capacity model and an example escrow credit calculation. Pricing for burst credits is a blended rate (reserved rate + 1.25x premium) and we offer a capped monthly spend for peace-of-mind.

Next steps: Ben will outline commercial terms for burst-escrow and Lauren can draft the SLA addendum. Would you prefer a fixed monthly burst allowance or a flexible escrow that can be top-up on demand?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: peregrine_capacity_model_v3.xlsx, Redwood_SLA-draft-20280729.pdf
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 16:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated pool + short bursts

Amy / Team — quick commercial note on burst escrow options: we normally offer two approaches.

1) Monthly burst allowance (recommended for predictable workloads): pre-purchase X GPU-hours that sit in an escrow. If you don't use them, they roll forward for up to 3 months. Overage billed at escrow unit price.

2) On-demand top-up (recommended for early-stage or variable patterns): no upfront commitment. Burst uses are billed at the on-demand premium. We can dial a hard cap and auto-notify your infra when spending hits thresholds.

For Peregrine's estimates (from Karthik's model), a conservative starting configuration is: 12 reserved + 8 monthly-burst-escrow GPUs (equivalent to ~192 GPU-hours/month at average utilization). That buys you ~4 sustained 30-minute 8x spikes across a month.

If procurement wants contractual language, I can produce an escrow addendum and sample invoice terms.

— Ben
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Cho <amy@peregrine.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 13:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated pool + short bursts

Amy — copying in a draft SLA snippet and the proposed autoscale rules (summary below). This will go into the Dedicated contract addendum: 

- SLO / prewarm: 99.5% of latency-sensitive requests served with no more than 250ms additional cold-start latency when utilizing prewarmed shoulder capacity.
- Burst activation: system will attempt to allocate ephemeral GPUs within 60s for fast-lane routes, subject to regional availability and mutual blackout windows.
- Eviction policy: preemptible ephemeral instances will be chosen first; reserved slab is last to be evicted. In event of global capacity pressure, Redwood will provide prioritized routing to degraded model variant (e.g., quantized variant) rather than dropping requests.
- Billing & credits: monthly escrow consumed first; overages billed at on-demand premium. We will include notification thresholds at 50%, 80%, 95% of escrow consumption.

Two operational asks from our side: (1) confirm a contact for on-call burst escalations (we suggest Peregrine name + 1 engineer), (2) provide a 2-week trial window for stress testing before the contract goes live.

I can fold these clauses into the SLA PDF and return a clean copy by Monday.

Thanks,
Lauren
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this aligns with our needs. A few clarifying points before we present to procurement: 

- Can Redwood provide an appendix that shows the math for the recommended 8 burst GPUs (the spreadsheet helps, but procurement wants a one-page rationale)?
- During a cross-regional launch (US + EU), how does regional availability impact the 60s fast-lane SLA? Do you reserve burst capacity per-region or is it pooled?
- For the 2-week trial, we want a controlled chaos test that includes simulated 10–30 minute 6–10x spikes. Will Redwood run the test jointly with our SREs and share telemetry?

If you can confirm the above and send the procurement-facing addendum we can aim to sign the addendum and start the trial in the week of Aug 12.

— Miguel
Director of Infrastructure, Peregrine Robotics
